payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-26
payload.summary:
**Bot traffic just crossed the human line**, and **Cloudflare** says the old ad-funded web may not survive the agent era; **Anthropic** plugged **Claude** into Apple’s Foundation Models stack, pushing a clean on-device-to-cloud handoff; on X, the mood swung from **Codex spreading beyond engineers** and travel-booking agent demos to a louder fight over AI regulation, identity checks, and who gets to control frontier models.

**机器人流量已经压过真人**，**Cloudflare** 直接把话挑明了：靠广告养活互联网这套，碰上 agent 可能真要改写；**Anthropic** 把 **Claude** 接进苹果 Foundation Models，端侧先跑、复杂任务再上云，这条产品线很实在；X 上也挺热闹，一边是 **Codex** 往工程圈外扩、一边是拿它去比价订日本行程，另一边则是 AI 监管、身份验证、前沿模型控制权吵得更凶了。

items.person_name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

sections.headline: **Cloudflare** says bots already beat humans online; **Cloudflare** 称机器人流量已超过真人
sections.body:
**Matt Turck** interviews **Cloudflare** CEO **Matthew Prince** on a sharp inflection point: bot and agent traffic has already passed human traffic in the first half of 2026, much earlier than Cloudflare expected. Prince argues the real pressure is not just more requests, but a different shape of demand, where one user task can trigger thousands of visits by agents. He ties that to a looming infrastructure surge across servers, networks, CPUs, GPUs, and memory, then pushes the bigger claim: the 28-year ad model of the web breaks when bots do the clicking.

**Matt Turck** 这期找来 **Cloudflare** CEO **Matthew Prince**，核心就一句：2026 年上半年，机器人和 agent 流量已经超过真人，而且比他们原先估得快得多。Prince 讲得很直白，麻烦不只是请求变多，而是流量形态变了，同一件事，人类可能点 5 个站，agent 会扫 5000 个。后面连着的是基础设施压力：服务器、网络、CPU、GPU、内存都得往上堆。更狠的一点是，他觉得互联网过去 28 年靠广告吃饭的模型碰上 bot 时代会出问题，因为 bot 根本不点广告。

sections.headline: **Claude** joins Apple Foundation Models in Swift; **Claude** 接进苹果 Foundation Models 的 Swift 工作流
sections.body:
**Anthropic** announced a new Swift package that lets Apple developers call **Claude** through Apple’s Foundation Models framework. The pitch is straightforward: use Apple’s native on-device models for fast local work like extraction or summarization, then hand off to **Claude** for harder jobs such as multi-step reasoning, code generation, web search, and tool use. Because Apple’s framework can emit typed Swift values, the Claude call starts from structured inputs rather than raw prompt text, with streaming and tool calls flowing back into the same SwiftUI view.

**Anthropic** 发了个新的 Swift 包，让苹果开发者能通过 Apple 的 Foundation Models framework 直接调 **Claude**。思路不绕：轻一点、快一点的事先在端上做，比如提取、摘要；一旦进入多步推理、写代码、查网页、跑工具这类重活，再切给 **Claude**。苹果这套能先产出类型化的 Swift 值，所以传给 Claude 的不是一坨原始用户文本，而是更干净的结构化输入；返回流、工具调用、结构化结果也都能直接回到同一个 SwiftUI 视图里。

sections.headline: Argues AI regulation is a geopolitical prisoner's dilemma / 认为 AI 监管本质上是地缘政治版囚徒困境
sections.body:
AI regulation is far less simple than it looks. It’s prisoners dilemma at insane scale. 

In theory if all leading AI labs globally agreed to the same process of review and slow down, then we’d get frontier intelligence at similar rates and it diffuses relatively evenly. 

If the US remains at the frontier at all times, and has heavy regulation on the release of intelligence then we end up with an economic and geopolitical edge because we can control who has access to frontier intelligence. 

If we delay model releases, however, and another player - specifically China - doesn’t slow down and has equally strong models (not now but soon?) then our delays end up advantaging their models and eventually their tech stack.

Now, the US could ban these models, but that actually only puts the US at a steeper disadvantage because other countries won’t have those bans. Then, from a relative competitiveness standpoint the US has now fallen behind even though it started in front.

So, none of this is as simple as it looks. At some point it’s a simple bet of can closed models remain at the frontier in perpetuity or is there a risk of any other player or market catching up or just not falling behind.

AI 监管远没有看上去那么简单。这是一个放大到离谱规模的囚徒困境。

理论上，如果全球主要 AI 实验室都同意走同一套审查和减速流程，那前沿智能的推进速度会比较接近，扩散也会相对均匀。

如果美国始终保持在前沿，同时又对智能的发布实施重监管，那我们就会获得经济和地缘政治优势，因为我们可以控制谁能接触到前沿智能。

但如果我们延迟模型发布，而另一方，尤其是中国，不减速，并且拿出了同样强的模型（现在还没有，但很快？），那我们的延迟最后反而会帮到他们的模型，最终也会帮到他们的技术栈。

美国当然可以禁这些模型，但那实际上只会让美国处在更不利的位置，因为别的国家不会有这些禁令。这样一来，从相对竞争力看，美国明明一开始领先，最后却会落后。

所以这事一点都不简单。说到底，就是在赌：闭源模型能不能一直守住前沿，还是说总会有别的参与者或市场追上来，哪怕不是全面超越，至少也不会掉队。

sections.headline: Says de facto AI regulation is already here / 认为事实上的 AI 监管已经落地
sections.body:
We now have de facto AI regulation. It’s not obvious why from here on out models that have certain levels of capability or are trained on certain compute sizes won’t have to be reviewed by the government before release. 

Realistically, as AI models became more and more powerful this was going to be inevitable (I think it’s too early, but here we are). So now it’s mostly just interesting to think about the implications and scenarios from here. A few would be:

* America gets to control who gets access to frontier intelligence and when. This generally works as long as we remain at the frontier at all times and don’t have a risk of being surpassed. At the moment we have a clear lead in frontier intelligence so this is a good bet, but lots of motivated parties would love to change that.

* This likely creates backlog of AI releases which means that we will see less rapid fire back and forth jumps in model progress. Bull/fine case is that we just get bigger step functions per release at a slower rate and we end up at the same point we would have. Bear case is those incremental smaller jumps were necessary for the continued flywheel of innovation. 

* Other countries likely have even more incentive to at least hedge their bets with sovereign AI strategies so aren’t dependent on access to US AI all times. Previously this was relatively moot because the alternative wasn’t good enough, but that could change out of necessity and what we’re seeing in China.

* Open weights obviously a big winner here as it becomes what likely sovereign AI gets built out on, and what (for now) can still be released to the market without the same controls. One interesting question would be how regulation eventually extends to open models, which would have its own set of long term consequences.

Anyway some big updates to everyone’s mental models of AI regulation as a result of the capabilities we’re now seeing in AI. Wild times.

我们现在已经有了事实上的 AI 监管。接下来，能力达到某个级别、或者训练算力达到某个规模的模型，发布前为什么不会需要政府审查，这件事并不显然。

现实点说，随着 AI 模型越来越强，这一步本来就迟早会来（我觉得现在还太早，但事情已经到了这一步）。所以现在更值得想的是，接下来会带来哪些影响和情景。比如：

* 美国可以控制谁能在什么时间拿到前沿智能。只要我们始终站在前沿、没有被超掉的风险，这套基本能成立。眼下我们在前沿智能上确实领先，所以这是一笔不错的赌注，但也有很多动力极强的参与者想改写这个局面。

* 这大概率会让 AI 发布排队，意味着模型进展不会再那样高频、来回猛跳。乐观一点看，就是每次发布的台阶更大、频率更慢，最后还是能走到同一个位置。悲观一点看，那些更小、更连续的增量，本来就是创新飞轮继续转下去所必需的。

* 其他国家大概率更有动力押注主权 AI，至少先做对冲，免得一直受制于美国 AI 的可得性。之前这个问题不算太要紧，因为替代方案还不够好；但出于现实需要，再加上中国这边已经发生的事，情况可能会变。

* 开放权重显然是赢家之一，因为主权 AI 很可能会建在这上面，而且目前它也还是能在没有同等控制的情况下放到市场上。更有意思的问题是，监管最终会怎么延伸到开放模型，那会带来另一套长期后果。

总之，AI 现在展现出来的能力，正在迫使大家重画自己脑子里的监管地图。确实挺野。

sections.headline: Says pure software startups now need a heretical view / 认为现在做纯软件创业得有很反常识的判断
sections.body:
It is stupidly hard to start a pure software company right now.

Customers don't want software, they want outcomes. So you end up having to do a lot of custom work for them. 

Anything horizontal is on a ticking clock.

Every customer wants to deeply customize.

There are opportunities.

But you need to have a very heretical 2-3 year view of the world in order to build something good.

现在做一家纯软件公司，难得离谱。

客户不要软件，他们要结果。所以你最后往往得替他们做很多定制活。

所有横向产品都像挂着倒计时。

每个客户都想深度定制。

机会当然有。

但你得对未来 2 到 3 年有一套很反常识的判断，才有可能做出像样的东西。
